title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.00460v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions. These benchmarks are also public and widely used online, which may be resulting in LLM memorization. Models may perform better on questions that they have seen before. It is also not evident whether smaller models, which are more locally deployable in HIPAA-compliant hospital settings, have achieved human performance. translated_title: 从小到大：评估语言模型中的医学推理、基准污染与模型规模
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）如今在回答医学考试题目方面已达到甚至超过专家水平，但目前尚不清楚这些分数究竟是反映了真正的临床能力，还是受到了提问格式（例如多选题与开放式题目的差异）、模型此前接触过这些基准测试以及题目难度的影响。这些基准测试是公开的，且在网上被广泛使用，这可能导致LLM产生记忆效应——模型在曾见过的题目上可能表现更好。此外，尚不清楚更适合在符合HIPAA合规要求的医院环境中本地部署的较小模型是否已达到人类水平。在本研究中，我们评估了来自六家领先厂商的十四个现有模型（每家厂商各选一个较小模型和一个较大模型，另加两个开放权重模型），在四个医学基准（MedQA-USMLE、MedMCQA、PubMedQA和MedBullets）的3,076道题目上，在标准多选……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过评估来自六家厂商的14个不同规模语言模型在四个医学基准共3,076道题目上的表现，考察医学考试成绩是否真实反映临床推理能力，还是受题目格式、基准污染（记忆效应）和模型规模的影响，并检验适合本地部署的小模型能否达到人类水平。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates fourteen LLMs of varying sizes from six providers on 3,076 questions across four medical benchmarks to determine whether their expert-level medical exam performance reflects true clinical reasoning or is confounded by benchmark contamination, question format, and model size, while assessing whether smaller locally deployable models reach human-level performance.
